title: How many days are in a thousand calendar years?
description: Every four hundredth year is a leap year after all. The video sorts a thousand calendar years into four kinds, counts the days, and compares them with the Earth.
teaching_notes: One idea: sort the years into four kinds by what divides them, count the days of each kind, and add. Watch for children who count every year divisible by four as a leap year.

source: Every 400th year is a leap year after all. Count the years of each kind in 1000 calendar years and find the total number of days.
video_script.why: The child has seen the calendar fall behind the Earth when the hundredth year loses its leap day, and now meets the final rule that every four hundredth year is a leap year.
video_script.substitution: the book's own thousand calendar years sorted into four kinds by what divides them, against the Earth's three hundred and sixty five point two four two two days a trip
video_script.anchor: A thousand calendar years sorted into four kinds by what divides them
video_script.wrong_answer: two hundred and fifty leap years
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip counts every year divisible by four as a leap year, so two hundred and fifty leap years in a thousand years. But eight of those years are divisible by one hundred and not by four hundred, and they get no leap day.
video_script.payoff_line: The days in a thousand years are now known.

final_answer.spoken: three hundred and sixty five thousand two hundred and forty two days, short by zero point two days

maths_rules: divisible by 400: 1000 ÷ 400 gives 2 years, each 366 days
divisible by 100 but not by 400: 10 − 2 = 8 years, each 365 days
divisible by 4 but not by 100: 250 − 10 = 240 years, each 366 days
Earth: 1000 × 365.2422 = 365242.2 days, so the calendar is short by 365242.2 − 365242 = 0.2 days
the slip: 250 leap years, when the leap years number 2 + 240 = 242
video_script.design: One idea: sort the years by what divides them, count the days of each kind, and add. Assumes the earlier videos on the calendar. Wrong idea: every year divisible by four is a leap year. The gap of zero point two stays hidden until the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, count the years of each kind.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A thousand divided by four hundred gives two years divisible by four hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A thousand divided by one hundred gives ten. Eight of those ten are not divisible by four hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>A thousand divided by four gives two hundred and fifty. Ten are divisible by one hundred, so two hundred and forty are not.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The remaining years are plain. A thousand take away two, eight and two hundred and forty leaves seven hundred and fifty.
